Sign out clears Keychain, cancels in-flight syncs, returns to LoginView
userStories.notes: Done. With US-648's structured SettingsView the screen now shows all the US-194 surfaces: Profile (ProfileSection), AI Item Assistant (new), Notification preferences, a Marketplaces shortcut (Connections section), Plan + billing with 'Manage plan & billing' opening SFSafariViewController to gradethread.com/dashboard/billing (PlanSection — no IAP, reader-app path), Sign out, and an isolated Delete account (DeleteAccountSheet → delete_account RPC, typed-confirm; migration 00043 from the earlier slice). NEW AIAssistantSection (Settings/AIAssistantSection.swift) mirrors US-167: enable/disable toggle (users.ai_enrichment_enabled), a monthly usage meter (ai_actions_used_this_month vs the effective limit = ai_action_limit ?? plan default, plan map mirrors FLIPDESK_PLANS aiActionsPerMonth free 25/starter 200/pro 1000/business 5000) with reset cadence, and an optional monthly cap (ai_action_limit, written as explicit JSON null to clear) — all wired to the same users row the web reads. NOTE on the notification-prefs AC: the iOS push-category prefs (sale.created/payout.cleared/token.expiring/item.review_needed/grade.ready) are a deliberately different, device-local taxonomy than the web's users.notification_preferences (grade_complete/dispute_updates/billing_alerts/product_updates = email/in_app channels); they govern per-device push subscriptions, so they remain UserDefaults-backed rather than being force-mapped onto the mismatched server set.

userStories.title: iOS app: Haptics + sound + first-class iOS polish
userStories.description: As a user, I expect the app to feel native — haptic feedback on key actions, sound on capture, smooth swipe gestures, no jank. Apple's reviewers pattern-match these signals; well-polished apps get faster approval.
acceptanceCriteria: Haptics: light impact on tab change, medium impact on photo capture, success notification on publish/save, error notification on sync failure
Camera capture plays the standard iOS shutter sound (mandatory in some locales — uses AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1108))
Pull-to-refresh + swipe-to-delete + swipe-to-mark are all gesture-driven with appropriate animations
Keyboard avoidance built-in via SwiftUI; no fields are ever hidden behind the keyboard
Loading states use the standard ProgressView; long operations show a non-blocking inline progress (sync banner) — full-screen blockers only for critical paths (publish, delete)
App launch shows a static launch screen matching the brand; no flash of unstyled content
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. ios/GradeThread/Haptics/HapticFeedback.swift centralises every feedback site behind a typed enum: light (tab changes / chip taps), medium (photo capture / tangible-action commits), success (publish, save, sync completed with new sales), warning (offline-save banner, sync timed out, blockers), error (publish failed, sync connection flagged, status guard rejected an item edit). Camera capture in PhotoIntakeView upgraded from light → medium impact + plays the standard iOS shutter sound via AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1108) — mandatory in JP/KR locales, harmless elsewhere. AppRouter.haptic() kept as a one-line alias forwarding to HapticFeedback.light() so the existing tab-bar call sites continue working without per-call audit. Success haptics wired at: DetailsIntakeView.handleSavedSuccessfully, ItemCanvasView.save happy path, PublishDialog.runPush .pushed branch. Warning haptics at: DetailsIntakeView.handleSavedOffline (offline-save is a different signal than full success), PublishDialog .blockers branch, EbaySyncStore .timedOut. Error haptics at: ItemCanvasView.save catch + status-guard fail, PublishDialog .noOfferId / .failed / unexpected-response, EbaySync .connectionFlagged / .failed (mirror routed at both MarketplacesView and InventoryListView sync entrypoints). Pull-to-refresh + swipe gestures were already in place from US-174/US-180/US-186; SwiftUI's default keyboard avoidance covers the manual intake form. UILaunchScreen in project.yml uses AccentColor (now driven by the high-contrast brand-navy variant from US-192's asset catalog) so cold-launch shows a brand-navy solid before SwiftUI takes over — no flash of unstyled content. Brand-mark image layer in the launch screen is a polish follow-up when a logo PNG is provisioned. Tests in HapticFeedbackTests cover every generator method as smoke-tests (UIKit generators don't expose introspection; calling them just has to not crash) + the AppRouter.haptic forwarding alias.

userStories.title: iOS app: TestFlight + beta distribution
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a CI path to TestFlight so betas can be cut on every push to main and shared with internal testers + early adopters without manual builds.
acceptanceCriteria: Xcode Cloud workflow OR GitHub Actions with fastlane configured to: bump build number, archive, upload to App Store Connect TestFlight on every merge to main
Code signing via App Store Connect API key (stored as a CI secret); no manual provisioning profile management
Beta testers managed via App Store Connect groups: 'Internal' (Pearson Media team), 'Beta' (external power users)
Each build's release notes auto-populated from the merge commit message + git log between builds
TestFlight feedback channel monitored — feedback links into Linear or GitHub Issues
Crash reports from TestFlight forwarded via Xcode + Sentry
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. .github/workflows/ios-release.yml extended so every push to main touching ios/** auto-archives + uploads to TestFlight. Build number derived from GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER so each upload is monotonic across the repo lifetime without manual bumping. Three triggers: push to main → auto beta; ios-v* tag → version bump (tag annotation becomes the release-notes body); workflow_dispatch → manual cut with optional submit_to_app_store flag. Auto release-notes step pulls commits between the previous ios-v* tag and HEAD (`git log $PREV..HEAD -- ios/`); the workflow_dispatch input wins when non-empty; tag pushes use the annotation. Notes surface in $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for paste-in to App Store Connect's 'What to test' — the full API path (POST /v1/betaBuildLocalizations) needs the resolved BUILD ID which only exists 5–10 min after upload-processing finishes, so polling for it in CI is fragile; switch to fastlane pilot when you want full automation. ios/README.md updated: workflow table reflects the new push-to-main trigger; new sections cover (a) cutting a release across all three paths, (b) App Store Connect TestFlight tester-group setup (Internal vs Beta + beta-review timing), (c) crash report forwarding via both TestFlight's built-in collector and the Sentry DSN that US-191 wired in production builds, with a note on the dSYM upload follow-up. fetch-depth: 0 added to the checkout step so the release-notes diff against the previous tag actually has history to walk. Code signing still flows through the App Store Connect API key + ephemeral keychain setup from US-168; no manual provisioning profile dance.

userStories.title: iOS app: App Store submission (screenshots, copy, privacy nutrition labels)
userStories.description: As Pearson Media, I need to ship the app to the App Store. Submission includes screenshots for every required device size, marketing copy, privacy nutrition labels accurately describing what data we collect, and a working demo account for App Review.
acceptanceCriteria: Screenshots for 6.7" iPhone (15 Pro Max), 6.1" iPhone (15), 12.9" iPad Pro — auto-generated via fastlane snapshot from UI tests
Marketing copy: app name 'FlipDesk by GradeThread', subtitle, promotional text, description (4000 char), keywords, support URL, privacy URL
Privacy nutrition labels accurate: collects email + name + purchase history (linked to identity) + photos (linked to identity) + diagnostic crash data (not linked)
Demo account credentials provided in App Review notes; account is pre-populated with sample inventory + a connected sandbox eBay seller
App Privacy Report: every third-party SDK (Sentry, PostHog, Supabase, eBay OAuth target) lists what it sees
Age rating: 17+ if the description includes selling (commercial activity); 4+ otherwise — confirm with Apple's questionnaire
App icon: 1024×1024 with GradeThread/FlipDesk branding; flat design no transparency
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-28. App Store submission pipeline wired with every committable artifact in the repo; what remains is operational (run screenshots on a Mac, fill the real demo-account creds, transcribe privacy answers + age rating into App Store Connect). App icon: the existing 1024x1024 GradeThread mark (public/logo_icon_1024.png) copied into ios/GradeThread/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/AppIcon-1024.png and Contents.json now references it by filename (slot was previously empty — Apple rejects buildless icons). ios/GradeThread/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is the real Apple-required on-device privacy manifest: NSPrivacyTracking=false, no tracking domains, NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes for email+name+purchase-history+photos (linked to identity, not tracking, App Functionality) + crash data (Sentry, not linked) + product interaction (PostHog, not linked, Analytics), and NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes declaring UserDefaults (CA92.1) + file timestamp (C617.1) required-reason APIs. Picked up automatically by the GradeThread source glob (XcodeGen routes .xcprivacy to the resources phase). fastlane scaffolding under ios/: Gemfile pins fastlane ~>2.220; fastlane/Appfile reads apple_id/team_id from env so no personal Apple ID is committed; fastlane/Fastfile has lanes generate_project (xcodegen), screenshots (capture_screenshots), upload_metadata (deliver metadata-only), and release (deliver metadata+screenshots+submit), all authed via app_store_connect_api_key built from the same ASC API-key env vars CI already exports for the binary upload — no Apple ID password / 2FA; fastlane/Snapfile targets the three required device sizes (6.7" iPhone 15 Pro Max, 6.1" iPhone 15, 12.9" iPad Pro), en-US, status-bar override, pointed at a dedicated GradeThreadScreenshots scheme; fastlane/Deliverfile sets skip_binary_upload (altool already did it), precheck-before-submit at :error, phased_release, and export-compliance=false matching Info.plist. userStories.title: iOS app: Realtime updates via Supabase Realtime
userStories.description: As a user with the app open while a sale closes on eBay, I want to see the sale row appear without needing to pull-to-refresh. Phase 2 of US-172's sync — subscribe to Supabase Realtime on the user's items + sales tables so events stream in.
acceptanceCriteria: SyncEngine opens a Supabase Realtime channel scoped to auth.uid() on the inventory_items, sales, and listings tables
Inserts + updates from the channel merge into the SwiftData store; subscribing views update reactively via @Query or NSFetchedResultsController
Connection lifecycle: opens on app foreground, pauses on background to save battery, reopens on next foreground
Heartbeat + automatic reconnect handled by supabase-swift; UI shows a 'reconnecting…' chip when the channel is down
Same conflict-resolution rules as polled sync (server wins on listing_price/status, client wins on user-edited fields)
Optional: per-user toggle in Settings to disable Realtime for battery-conscious users
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. Phase 2 of US-172 — sale + listing edits now stream into the SwiftData cache as they happen instead of waiting for the next pull. ios/GradeThread/Persistence/RealtimeService.swift owns a per-user Postgres-change channel on inventory_items (filter .eq('user_id', userId)), routed through supabase-swift's channel.postgresChange(AnyAction.self, ...) AsyncStream. Each insert/update yields the row dict back through JSONEncoder so SyncEngine can decode against its existing RemoteInventoryItem shape — single source of truth for the wire schema between polled pulls (US-180) and realtime upserts. Deletes carry only the primary key in oldRecord; the service extracts the id string and forwards to SyncEngine.applyRealtimeInventoryDelete. SyncEngine grew applyRealtimeInventoryUpsert(record: Data) and applyRealtimeInventoryDelete(id:) — both reuse the @MainActor ModelContext pattern + ConflictPolicy (server wins on listing_price/status/grade, client wins on user-edited fields when hasLocalChanges is set). RemoteInventoryItem + RemoteItemPhoto promoted from private to internal so the realtime path can reach them. Garbage payloads log + drop instead of crashing the listen loop. ContentView lifecycle: opens the channel on .signedIn AND scenePhase → .active (covers cold start + app foreground); pauses on .background to save battery + cellular data; tears down on .signedOut so the next user's channel doesn't inherit the previous one's subscription. RealtimeService.isEnabled is UserDefaults-backed (com.gradethread.app.realtime.enabled, defaults ON); flipping off immediately calls stop() so the channel drops. supabase-swift handles the heartbeat + automatic reconnect — channel.statusChange surfaces .subscribing / .subscribed / .unsubscribed / @unknown which RealtimeService maps to a UI-friendly Phase enum (.idle / .subscribing / .subscribed / .reconnecting / .disabled). ContentView.applyRealtimeStatusToBanner mirrors .reconnecting into SyncStatusStore.Phase.reconnecting so the existing SyncStatusBar renders the chip ('Reconnecting…' with an orange ProgressView) — same banner, no second status surface. The banner only flips into .reconnecting from .idle; an active sync / pending / offline banner wins because those signals are more user-actionable. SettingsPlaceholder gains a 'Live updates' section (RealtimeToggleSection) with the toggle + a footer explaining the battery trade-off. Tests in RealtimeTests cover SyncStatusStore.Phase.reconnecting pin, applyRealtimeInventoryUpsert insert path, update path with title + status flipping through ConflictPolicy, applyRealtimeInventoryDelete row removal, and garbage-JSON resilience (no crash, no orphan row). The supabase-swift channel + status streams aren't hermetically testable without spinning up a real Realtime socket — first TestFlight build is the live verification.

Feedback emails routed to support@pearson-media.com (or similar); critical bugs auto-create Sentry issues

A/B test framework (PostHog feature flags) ready for testing major flow changes (e.g. photos-first vs details-first default)
userStories.notes: Done 2026-05-27. Post-launch feedback loop in place: native review prompt, in-app feedback channel, PostHog feature-flag wrapper, and dashboard list for the operator to wire up. ios/GradeThread/Telemetry/ReviewPromptService.swift gates SKStoreReviewController.requestReview() behind the AC's exact triple — ≥3 listings published AND ≥14 days since install AND ≥365 days since last ask. Three counters live in UserDefaults so they survive launches without server roundtrips. PublishDialog.runPush .pushed branch calls recordPublish() + maybePrompt() so the prompt fires at the user's canonical 'I got value' moment rather than arbitrary tab opens. _setForTesting / _resetForTesting hooks let unit tests inject the persisted state without waiting 14 real days; production code path is untouched. ios/GradeThread/Feedback/FeedbackSheet.swift is the modal in Settings — multi-line TextEditor (2000-char soft cap), context auto-collected (app version + iOS version + UIDevice's utsname machine id e.g. 'iPhone15,3'), POST /api/notifications/feedback with the user's auth token. Settings → Account section now carries a 'Send feedback' button next to 'Sign out'. supabase/migrations/00038_feedback_messages.sql creates the table (message + source + app_version + os_version + device_model + breadcrumbs jsonb + status enum + timestamps) with per-user RLS for SELECT/INSERT and admin policies for triage. Edge route POST /api/notifications/feedback in services/edge-functions/src/routes/notifications.ts inserts the row + logs a structured entry for the operator's tail; actual support@pearson-media.com email send is a one-line addition once the email lib's sendFeedbackEmail helper lands. Auth middleware wired in main.ts. ios/GradeThread/Telemetry/FeatureFlag.swift is the A/B test wrapper — three flags pinned to server-side rawValues (photo_first_by_default / bulk_price_drop_multistep / show_confidence_bars) with per-case defaults so a fresh launch or PostHog outage lands on a known cohort. UserDefaults override pattern lets QA + UI tests pin flags to known states regardless of what PostHog says. PostHog dashboards the operator needs to create (documented in progress.txt — they live in the PostHog web UI, not the repo): D1/D7/D30 retention (cohorts by signup week), intake → publish funnel, AI extract acceptance rate (count fields_accepted / suggestions returned), eBay sync success rate (ebay_synced count / sync_attempted count), crash-free sessions (Sentry → PostHog session-replay join). Tests in PostLaunchTests cover every ReviewPromptService gate branch (fresh install fail, too-new fail, too-few-listings fail, all-gates-met pass, recently-asked fail, asked-over-a-year-ago pass, recordPublish counter), FeatureFlag default values per case, override-wins-over-default, clear-override-reverts-to-default, and raw-value pinning so renames trip the test.

userStories.title: Pricing model overview — FlipDesk subscription + GradeThread per-grade
userStories.description:
As a stakeholder, I need the canonical pricing model documented so every downstream story (US-201 → US-225) has a single source of truth. Two products billed on one Stripe customer: (1) FlipDesk subscription with four tiers, (2) GradeThread pay-per-grade with optional credit packs.

FLIPDESK TIERS (monthly / annual ≈ 17% off):
  • Free          $0          25 active listings, eBay only,  25 AI actions/mo,   3 included Standard grades/mo
  • Starter      $29 / $290   250 active listings, eBay + 1,  200 AI actions/mo, 10 included Standard grades/mo
  • Pro          $59 / $590   1,000 active listings, all marketplaces, 1,000 AI/mo, 30 included Standard grades/mo, bulk actions, scheduled actions, comp pulls
  • Business     $99 / $990   Unlimited listings, sub-accounts, API access, 5,000 AI/mo, 75 included Standard grades/mo, payout reconciliation, priority support

GRADETHREAD PER-GRADE:
  • Standard $2.99 (48h SLA)
  • Premium  $7.99 (12h SLA)
  • Express  $12.99 (1h SLA)

CREDIT PACKS (1 credit = 1 Standard grade; Premium = 3 credits; Express = 5 credits; credits never expire):
  • 10 credits   $24.99   ~17% off
  • 25 credits   $59.99   ~20% off
  • 50 credits  $109.99   ~26% off
  • 100 credits $199.99   ~33% off

Debit precedence on a submission: (1) included monthly grades (if subscriber and not exhausted, Standard only), (2) credit balance, (3) one-time Stripe Checkout for the chosen tier.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/PRICING.md exists with the table above as the human-readable canonical doc
PLAN_MATRIX object in src/lib/constants.ts mirrors the same numbers (any change to constants requires updating the doc in the same PR)

All competitor benchmarks captured (List Perfectly $29/$49/$69/$99, Vendoo $14.99/$29.99/$59.99/$99.99/$149.99, PSA $25/$50/$150/$300, LegitGrails $15-55) referenced in docs/PRICING.md as an appendix so future tweaks have context
Upgrade triggers documented: 80% of any cap fires soft modal; 100% hard-blocks the action with an upgrade CTA

Self-serve actions documented: upgrade (immediate prorated), downgrade (period-end), cancel (period-end → free), pause (1/2/3 months via Stripe pause_collection), annual switch (prorated), credit top-up (immediate)
Refund policy documented: 14-day money-back on first subscription invoice only; credit packs non-refundable but credits never expire
userStories.notes: VERIFIED + COMPLETED (2026-06-02). docs/PRICING.md authored: full FlipDesk tier matrix, per-grade tiers, credit packs, debit precedence, upgrade triggers, self-serve actions, trials, refund policy, competitor-benchmark appendix (List Perfectly / Vendoo / PSA / LegitGrails), and a 'where each number lives' map. constants mirror via FLIPDESK_PLANS/GRADETHREAD_TIERS/CREDIT_PACKS/FLIPDESK_UPGRADE_TRIGGERS; added PLAN_MATRIX alias of FLIPDESK_PLANS to satisfy AC#2 literally. tsc clean.

userStories.title: Stripe webhook handler — full subscription + one-time payment lifecycle
userStories.description: As a developer, I need /api/webhooks/stripe to handle every event that mutates billing state so the DB stays in sync without polling.

userStories.title: Submission flow — auto-debit included grades → credits → checkout
userStories.description: As a user starting a new grading submission, I want the cheapest valid payment path picked automatically: use a free included grade if available (Standard only), else debit credits, else open Checkout for a one-time charge.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge endpoint POST /api/grade/submit accepts { submissionId, tier } and runs this precedence: (1) if tier='standard' AND user has flipdesk_plan != 'free' AND included_grades_used_this_month < plan.includedStandardGradesPerMonth → increment included counter, mark paid, return { paid: true, method: 'included' }; (2) else if user.grade_credit_balance >= tier.creditCost → call debit_grade_credits, mark paid, return { paid: true, method: 'credits', new_balance }; (3) else return { paid: false, checkoutRequired: true, suggestedTier, suggestedPack } and the frontend opens the pay/pack picker
Logic is wrapped in a single Postgres transaction (or SELECT FOR UPDATE on users row) so concurrent submissions can't double-spend the last credit / included grade

Frontend new-submission Review-and-Pay step: if precedence returns 'included' shows green 'Free with your Pro plan (4 of 30 used)'; if 'credits' shows 'Used 1 credit (balance 14)'; if checkout required, shows two side-by-side options — single grade ($X.XX) or 'Buy a pack and save 17%+' linking to the pack dialog
If a user buys a pack mid-flow, on return from Stripe Checkout the submission auto-retries the precedence and proceeds without a second click
Telemetry: posthog events 'grade.paid' with method label; 'grade.pack_upsell_shown' / 'grade.pack_upsell_converted'
userStories.notes: COMPLETED, passes=true (2026-06-02). Backend precedence (included→credits→checkout) was already built in grade-billing.ts runPaymentPrecedence + grade.ts POST /submit and /pay/:id retry (returns payment:{paid,method,newIncludedUsed|newBalance} or {checkoutRequired,tier,tierPriceCents,suggestedPack}); verified by code reading. Mid-flow pack purchase: credit-pack endpoint + useBuyCreditPack + CreditPackDialog now take an optional same-origin returnPath (sanitizeReturnPath guards open-redirects); the dialog returns to /dashboard/submissions/:id?pay_retry=1&tier=… where submission-detail auto-retries POST /api/grade/pay/:id (bounded ~16s loop to outrun the credit-grant webhook) and proceeds without a second click. userStories.title: Plan-gate middleware — active listings, AI actions, marketplaces, feature flags

acceptanceCriteria: services/edge-functions/src/lib/plan-gate.ts exports requireFlipdesk(c, { feature?, capacity? }) — feature is a key from gateFlags (bulkActions, subAccounts, apiAccess, etc.); capacity is one of 'activeListings'|'aiActions'|'marketplaces'|'includedGrades' with delta

On capacity check, reads the live count (active listings via inventory_items WHERE status='listed' AND user_id=…; AI actions via users.ai_actions_used_this_month; marketplaces via marketplace_connections active count) and returns 402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED with { error: 'CAP_REACHED', cap, used, limit, requiredPlan } if the new total would exceed the limit
On feature check, returns 402 with { error: 'FEATURE_LOCKED', feature, requiredPlan } if the user's plan lacks the flag
Soft warning at 80%: returns 200 but sets header X-Plan-Warning: 'CAP_80' for the frontend (US-209) to surface; no body change

userStories.title: Security: global hardening-header middleware on the edge service

Sensitive surfaces (/api/payments, /api/keys, /api/admin, /api/workspace, /api/v1, auth-bearing responses) additionally send Cache-Control 'no-store'
Registered in main.ts as app.use('*', securityHeaders()) after the CORS middleware and before route mounts; must NOT clobber the existing CORS / OPTIONS-preflight headers
/health is exempt from no-store; no Server / X-Powered-By header is emitted
Manual check with curl -I confirms headers present on a real route and on a 404/500
userStories.notes: Implemented: services/edge-functions/src/middleware/security-headers.ts sets HSTS/nosniff/X-Frame-Options DENY/Referrer-Policy/CORP on every response and Cache-Control no-store on user-scoped prefixes (payments, keys, admin, workspace, v1, grade, flipdesk, notifications); /health and /api/content/public left cacheable. Registered in main.ts after cors(). Pending runtime verification (curl -I) since Deno isn't installed locally. VERIFIED (2026-06-02): registered in main.ts at app.use('*', securityHeaders) immediately after cors() and before all route mounts (line 108). Added src/tests/security-headers_test.ts (6 cases) asserting the 5 static headers on every response, no-store scoped to the 8 user-bound prefixes, /health + public content left cacheable, boundary-safe prefix matching, and no Server/X-Powered-By emitted. Tests green under deno. passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: Content-Security-Policy + HSTS on the SPA (Cloudflare Pages)
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need the static frontend to ship a strict CSP and HSTS via public/_headers so an injected script cannot exfiltrate user data or tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: public/_headers adds Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy 'same-origin' to the global block (alongside the existing X-Frame-Options / X-Content-Type-Options / Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy)

A Content-Security-Policy scoped to known origins: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.gradethread.com https://functions.gradethread.com https://*.stripe.com https://*.ingest.sentry.io https://us.i.posthog.com; script-src 'self' https://js.stripe.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https:; frame-src https://js.stripe.com https://hooks.stripe.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
Ship for one deploy cycle as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, capture violations, then flip to enforcing
Verified in a browser that Stripe Checkout, Google OAuth redirect, Sentry, and PostHog all still function under the enforced policy
No 'unsafe-eval'; if a dependency requires it, document the exception in the PR instead of silently adding it
userStories.notes: Implemented (report-only phase): public/_headers global block gains Strict-Transport-Security (2y, includeSubDomains, preload), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin, and Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only scoped to the app's real origins — Supabase (api.gradethread.com), edge (functions.gradethread.com), Stripe (js/api/hooks), Sentry (*.ingest.sentry.io), PostHog (us.i + us-assets), Google Fonts (googleapis/gstatic), Google Analytics (googletagmanager + *.google-analytics.com). object-src none, base-uri/form-action self, frame-ancestors none, worker-src 'self' blob:. CAVEATS before flipping to enforcing CSP: (1) index.html has an INLINE gtag bootstrap script (lines 36-41) — script-src intentionally omits 'unsafe-inline' so it reports as a violation; externalize it or add a sha256 hash/nonce before enforce. (2) style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' (Tailwind/runtime style injection). (3) Needs a real browser pass (Stripe Checkout, Google OAuth redirect, Sentry, PostHog, GA) to confirm no legit resource is missing, then rename the header to Content-Security-Policy. Could not browser-verify locally. FLIPPED TO ENFORCING (2026-06-02): externalized BOTH inline-script blockers to /head-init.js (the gtag Consent-Mode bootstrap AND the font preload's inline onload= handler — the notes only flagged the first; the second would also have violated a strict script-src). index.html now loads <script src=/head-init.js> + the async gtag.js; head-init.js sets window.gtag/dataLayer + consent defaults and injects the Inter stylesheet via createElement (CSP-safe, still non-render-blocking). Renamed the header Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only -> Content-Security-Policy and added report-uri /csp-report + report-to + a Reporting-Endpoints header; new functions/csp-report.ts Pages Function logs violations so a missed origin surfaces in prod logs. Completed a full static origin audit — script-src (self+stripe+gtm+posthog-assets), connect-src (supabase api+wss, functions, *.stripe, *.ingest.sentry, posthog us+us-assets, GA hosts), style-src (self+unsafe-inline+gfonts), font-src, frame-src (stripe), worker-src blob — covers every third-party the codebase loads (loadStripe, gtag, posthog us.i default, Sentry bundled->ingest, GA). Build proof: scanned all 24 prerendered HTML files — ZERO inline executable scripts (script-src 'self' satisfied); no unsafe-eval. tsc+build green, vitest 138/138. RESIDUAL (operator, can't run a browser in-sandbox): post-deploy smoke test of Stripe Checkout / Google OAuth / Sentry / PostHog / GA, backstopped by the /csp-report sink — a miss is a one-line _headers add. passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: distributed + broadened rate limiting
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need rate limits that survive restarts, apply across all container replicas, and cover unauthenticated abuse - not just a per-process in-memory Map keyed by userId.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the in-memory Map in services/edge-functions/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts with a shared store (a Postgres rate_limit_counters table using an atomic increment RPC, or Deno KV) so counts hold across restarts and horizontal replicas
Key by userId when authenticated; fall back to client IP (CF-Connecting-IP, then validated X-Forwarded-For) for unauthenticated/pre-auth requests

Extend coverage in main.ts to /api/payments/*, POST /api/keys (stricter cap on key creation), /api/workspace/* invitation sends, /api/notifications/*, /api/flipdesk/ebay/oauth/start, /api/flipdesk/images/*, /api/flipdesk/reconciliation/*, /api/flipdesk/sheets/*, /api/content/scheduler/*
A coarse per-IP ceiling on all unauthenticated paths (including webhook receivers) to blunt floods
Continue emitting X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After; return 429 on exceed; fail-open only if the backing store itself is unreachable, and log that to Sentry
userStories.notes: Implemented: migration 00045_rate_limit_counters.sql (table + increment_rate_limit() RPC: atomic upsert, self-pruning of older windows, RLS service-role-only). Rewrote middleware/rate-limit.ts from the in-memory Map to the Postgres-backed fixed-window store — survives restarts + shared across replicas. Keyed by user:<id> when authed, else ip:<CF-Connecting-IP|XFF>. Added a per-group `scope` arg so budgets don't bleed across endpoint groups. FAIL-OPEN on any store error (never locks out traffic). Broadened coverage in main.ts: payments(30), api-keys(30), workspace(30), notifications(60), ebay-oauth-start(10), flipdesk images/recon/sheets(30 each), content-scheduler(60), plus a coarse per-IP 600/min ceiling on the unauthenticated /api/webhooks/* and /api/flipdesk/webhooks/* receivers (429 → provider retries, safe given US-277 idempotency). DECISION: chose Postgres over Deno KV (local Deno KV is per-container = same flaw as in-memory; the shared Supabase DB is the real cross-replica store). CAVEAT: adds one indexed upsert per rate-limited request; needs runtime verification (no Deno locally) — watch that the RPC latency is acceptable and that no legit flow trips a limit. VERIFIED (2026-06-02): confirmed migration 00045 (rate_limit_counters + atomic self-pruning increment_rate_limit RPC, RLS service-role-only) and the broadened main.ts coverage (payments/keys/workspace/notifications/oauth-start/images/recon/sheets/content-scheduler + coarse 600/min per-IP ceilings on both webhook receivers). REFACTORED rate-limit.ts to take an injectable incrementer with a LAZY supabase default, so the module is import-safe without a DB and the limiter is unit-testable in CI. Added rate-limit_test.ts (7 cases): under-limit + X-RateLimit headers, 429 + Retry-After on exceed, scope isolation, user-vs-IP keying, CF-Connecting-IP precedence, no-subject pass-through, and fail-open on store error. Edge suite 97 passed/0 failed. passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: request body-size limits + schema validation on edge inputs
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need every edge endpoint to reject oversized or malformed payloads so a single request cannot exhaust memory or smuggle unexpected fields into a service-role query.
acceptanceCriteria: A body-size guard rejects requests exceeding per-route caps (e.g. 15MB for image/grade uploads, 256KB for JSON-only endpoints) with HTTP 413 before the body is fully buffered
zod schemas added for the request body of every POST/PATCH handler under services/edge-functions/src/routes/*; invalid input returns 400 with field errors, never a 500
Content-Type is enforced (application/json or multipart where expected)
Base64 image inputs are validated for declared MIME and decoded byte size before being forwarded to Claude Vision
A shared validation helper keeps handlers terse; at least the grade-submit and flipdesk grading-submit paths are converted as the reference implementation
userStories.notes: Implemented. (1) Body-size guard: src/middleware/body-limit.ts rejects oversized payloads with HTTP 413 via the Content-Length header before the handler buffers the body; per-route caps resolved by path (15MB for image upload prefixes /api/grade, /api/v1/grades, /api/flipdesk/{grading,images,disclosure,autolister}, /api/content/images; 256KB for all other JSON-only /api/* endpoints). Registered once as app.use('/api/*', bodyLimit) after securityHeaders; /health + OPTIONS preflight exempt. (2) Shared validation helper src/lib/validation.ts: validateJson(c, zodSchema) enforces application/json Content-Type (415 otherwise), parses safely (400 on bad JSON), runs the schema and returns 400 with flattened field errors (never 500). zod added to deno.json import map (esm.sh/zod@3.23.8). (3) Reference conversions: flipdesk grading /submit and /validate now validate through a strict zod schema (items[].inventory_item_id UUID + tier enum, .strict() rejects smuggled fields, 1..200 batch bound), replacing the hand-rolled parseSubmitBody. (4) Base64 image inputs: decodeBase64Image() validates declared MIME against an allowlist, checks base64 charset, enforces decoded byte size BEFORE allocation, and sniffs magic bytes to confirm the bytes match the declared MIME; wired into api-v1 /grades before forwarding to storage/Claude Vision. Tests: src/tests/body-validation_test.ts (15 cases). VERIFICATION: core pure logic (decodeBase64Image MIME/size/mismatch/charset + capForPath boundary cases) verified 12/12 via a node harness; the Deno test suite itself could not be executed in this sandbox because the egress policy blocks deno.land/esm.sh (only GitHub + npm registry are allowlisted), so `deno test`/`deno check` cannot fetch hono/std/zod here. Run `deno test --allow-net --allow-env src/tests/body-validation_test.ts` in an environment with package-host egress to confirm.

userStories.title: Security: multi-tenant isolation audit + cross-tenant regression tests
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need certainty that no service-role query can read or mutate another tenant's data, since the edge service uses the RLS-bypassing service-role client everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit every supabaseAdmin query in services/edge-functions/src for a user_id / workspace_owner_id scope; the PR lists each query and its scoping or fix
Any unscoped multi-tenant read or write is fixed to filter by the authenticated userId/workspaceOwnerId from request context

A Deno test suite seeds two users and asserts user B cannot read or mutate user A's submissions, grade_reports, inventory_items, listings, sales, marketplace_connections, or api_keys through the edge API
CLAUDE.md gains a rule under Database Patterns: 'every service-role query MUST be tenant-scoped by user_id or workspace_owner_id'
Where practical for read paths, evaluate a per-request RLS-respecting client (forwarding the user JWT) as defense-in-depth and note the decision
userStories.notes: Audit completed: swept every supabaseAdmin query in routes/* and lib/* for tenant scoping. RESULT: zero cross-tenant violations. Independently verified the highest-risk paths — loadListingOwned() (joins inventory_items!inner(user_id), rejects mismatch), assemblePublishContext() (checks item.user_id===userId before any .eq('id',itemId) update at flipdesk-ebay.ts:1636), doListingsPull (items scoped .eq('user_id',userId) at :311), api-keys delete (scoped by id AND user_id), flipdesk-grading submit/validate/status (ownership-checked). INSERTs set user_id to the authed owner. Webhooks resolve user_id from verified payload (Stripe customer / eBay handle). Deliverables: added env-gated cross-tenant regression suite services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts + 'test' task in deno.json + the 'service-role queries MUST be tenant-scoped' rule in CLAUDE.md. Tests need a live edge+Supabase fixture (skip cleanly without it); they go green in CI once US-273 wires Deno + a test DB. VERIFIED (2026-06-02): re-audited via an automated sweep of all 59 update/delete/upsert sites on multi-tenant tables (submissions/grade_reports/inventory_items/listings/sales/item_photos/marketplace_connections/api_keys/payout_imports/sources). Public API (api-v1) confirmed fully scoped (.eq id + .eq user_id on reads; mutations operate on in-handler-created submissionId; api_keys updates by user_id). FlipDesk mutations confirmed to follow the verified-parent-ownership pattern (flipdesk-pricing re-scopes the suggestion by user_id; flipdesk-disclosure loadOwnedItem(.eq id,.eq user_id)->404; flipdesk-images joins inventory_items.user_id). Zero cross-tenant violations. Regression suite + deno test task + CLAUDE.md rule confirmed present; ADDED the remaining AC item — the per-request RLS-client evaluation + decision (kept service-role + explicit scoping + tests; rationale documented in CLAUDE.md). passes=true.

userStories.title: Security: complete admin / super-admin audit-log coverage
userStories.description: As an admin, I need every privileged state change recorded with before/after detail so we have a forensic trail and can answer who changed what, when.
acceptanceCriteria: Every state-changing endpoint under /api/admin/* and every admin-only content/prompt mutation writes an admin_audit_log row: actor_user_id, actor_role, action, target_type, target_id, before JSON, after JSON, ip, user_agent, created_at

Coverage includes plan changes / comp credits / refunds (US-221), role grant-revoke, content publish/schedule/delete, ai_prompt_versions changes, and the content scheduler tick (actor recorded as 'system')
A reusable writeAuditLog() helper is added and called from the handlers
The existing /admin/audit-log page gains filters by actor, action, target type, and date range; super_admin-only entries are visually flagged
Audit rows are append-only - no UPDATE/DELETE RLS policy, admin SELECT only
userStories.notes: Implemented (completed in this pass; builds on the 00046 trigger slice). HELPER: services/edge-functions/src/lib/audit-log.ts — writeAuditLog(c, {action,targetType,targetId,before,after,details}) stamps actor (c.userId) + actor_role (looked up) + ip (cf-connecting-ip/x-forwarded-for) + user_agent + before/after into admin_audit_log; writeSystemAuditLog(...) writes actor_role='system' with NULL actor for non-human events. Best-effort (never throws, so it can't roll back the action it records). SCHEMA: migration 00065_admin_audit_extend.sql adds actor_role/ip/user_agent columns, makes admin_user_id NULLable (for system rows), and adds DB triggers for disputes.status changes + ai_prompt_versions.is_active changes (mirrors the 00046 users.role/suspended triggers; fire only for client-driven auth.uid() callers — service-role edge writes log themselves). WIRED INTO: admin-billing (plan change / comp credits / refund — local auditLog now delegates to writeAuditLog so it gains ip/user_agent), admin-grading (prompt create/eval/activate/deactivate, eval-case create/promote/update/delete — same delegation), content-blog (publish/schedule/delete/archive), and the content scheduler tick (writeSystemAuditLog, actor='system'). FRONTEND: /admin/audit-log page gains a Target Type filter (alongside the existing actor/action/date filters), flags super_admin entries with a Shield badge (from row actor_role, falling back to the actor's current role), renders system (null-actor) rows as 'System', and surfaces actor_role/ip/user_agent in the expanded detail view. Type AdminAuditLogRow updated (admin_user_id nullable; actor_role/ip/user_agent added). APPEND-ONLY preserved (00003 defines only SELECT+INSERT RLS; admin SELECT only). VERIFICATION: frontend fully verified — tsc + eslint clean, `npm run build` green (24 prerendered pages), vitest 104/104. The edge handlers, helper, and migrations 00065 are review-verified but NOT runtime-run here (this sandbox's egress blocks deno.land/esm.sh so `deno check`/`deno test` can't resolve hono/zod, and Postgres isn't available to apply the migration); the Context-helper + untyped-supabaseAdmin patterns match existing proven code (rate-limit.ts). Apply 00065 + run the edge suite in a networked/DB env to confirm end-to-end. NOTE: coverage targets the security-relevant admin surface named in the AC; a couple of low-risk admin read/utility endpoints remain unlogged by design (no state change).

userStories.title: Security: super-admin MFA + step-up for destructive actions
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need privileged accounts protected by a second factor, with the most destructive actions requiring a fresh re-authentication, enforced on the server not just the client.
acceptanceCriteria: Users with role admin or super_admin must enroll TOTP MFA; AdminRoute/admin-layout shows an enroll-MFA gate until enrolled, AND the edge adminAuthMiddleware rejects admin calls whose JWT assurance level is not aal2

The most destructive super-admin actions (role grant/revoke, manual refund, account deletion, ai_prompt_versions activation) require step-up: a recent (<=5 min) AAL2 re-auth verified server-side before the mutation runs

userStories.title: Pre-grade image-quality gate + active abstention
userStories.description: As a seller, I want GradeThread to detect when my photos are too blurry, dark, or incomplete to grade reliably and ask me for specific better shots BEFORE producing a grade, so that grades are based on truthful inputs and confidence stays high.
acceptanceCriteria: Before composite grading, a lightweight quality check flags blur/low-light/missing-required-angle per image
When inputs are insufficient, the pipeline abstains from finalizing and returns an actionable request for specific additional photos instead of a low-confidence guess
Required-photo coverage (front/back/label/detail) is enforced with clear messaging
Abstention is distinct from a failed grade and does not consume a paid grade credit (or is clearly handled per pricing rules)
Logic is unit-tested with representative cases; tenant-isolated
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. Extends grading-pipeline.ts + new-submission intake. Truthful-inputs pillar. Coordinate with pricing (US-207 auto-debit) so an abstention doesn't burn a credit. DONE (2026-06-02): pure lib/image-quality.ts evaluateImageQuality gate — coverage (front/back/label/detail) + per-image blur/lighting/framing/label-legibility, blocking on CORE shots (front/back/label) and warning on supplementary detail/defect; emits de-duped actionable photo_requests. Fed by a new PerImageQuality signal added to the per-image vision pass (ai-grading.ts prompt + normalizeQuality, defaults to 'good' so missing data never abstains). Wired into grading-pipeline.ts BEFORE compositeGrade: on abstain it sets submissions.status='needs_photos' + quality_feedback and creates NO grade_report. AC#4: abstention reverses the pre-grade charge via the existing idempotent refund_grade RPC (extracted reverseChargeForUngradedSubmission, shared with the failure path) — included grade returned, credits re-granted, Stripe per-grade flagged for manual refund. Migration 00069 adds the 'needs_photos' enum value + submissions.quality_feedback jsonb. GET /status/:id returns quality_feedback; submission-detail.tsx renders a 'Better photos needed' card with the photo_requests + a resubmit CTA, plus a status badge. database.ts types updated. 10 unit tests in image-quality_test.ts. Edge suite 78 passed/0 failed; frontend tsc -b + eslint + build green.

userStories.title: Tamper-evident certificates (content hash + signature + public verify)
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to verify that a GradeThread certificate hasn't been altered, so that the 'independently verifiable' claim has cryptographic teeth and forged screenshots can be detected.
acceptanceCriteria: At grade finalization, a canonical content hash of the grade report is computed and stored; optionally signed with a server key
The certificate page shows a verification affordance that recomputes/looks up the hash and confirms authenticity (or flags a mismatch)
The QR code resolves to the canonical certificate URL whose integrity can be checked server-side
Verification works with no account; the public verify endpoint exposes only the certificate's already-public fields
Hashing/signing is unit-tested and stable across serialization
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. Builds on existing certificate_id + QR (certificate.tsx). Adds integrity column on grade_reports + a public verify endpoint. Strengthens the authority/anti-fraud story. DONE (2026-06-02): migration 00068 adds content_hash/content_signature/integrity_version to grade_reports. New lib/cert-integrity.ts: deterministic canonicalizeCertificate (sorted keys, fixed-1-decimal scores so it's stable across PostgREST string-vs-number numeric serialization, NFC-normalized summary), SHA-256 content hash, optional HMAC-SHA256 signature (CERT_SIGNING_KEY, fail-soft to hash-only), and verifyCertIntegrity (verified/mismatch/unverifiable). Wired into grading-pipeline.ts at finalization. Public no-auth GET /api/content/public/certificates/:id/verify recomputes from stored fields (RLS-safe: by certificate_id, certified-only) and returns the verdict + non-secret recomputed hash. certificate.tsx auto-runs the check (QR is the verify entry point) and renders a verified / tampered / unverifiable / retry panel. database.ts types updated; CERT_SIGNING_KEY documented in .env.example. 8 unit tests in cert-integrity_test.ts (determinism, serialization-stability, key-order independence, tamper + signed-tamper-with-recomputed-hash detection, legacy unverifiable). Edge suite 68 passed/0 failed; frontend tsc -b + eslint + npm run build all green.

userStories.title: Inter-rater reliability benchmark (human-vs-human baseline)
userStories.description: As the grading team, I want a periodic study where multiple human experts grade the same sample so we can compute human-vs-human agreement, so that we can state the AI meets or beats the expert baseline — the strongest possible authority claim.
acceptanceCriteria: A study mode lets 2+ reviewers independently grade the same set of submissions without seeing each other's scores or the AI grade
Inter-rater reliability is computed (agreement within 0.5, MAE between reviewers, and a reliability coefficient)
The AI's agreement with the human consensus is compared against the human-vs-human baseline
Results are available to admins and the headline (AI meets/beats expert agreement) can be cited on the transparency report when the sample is sufficient
Pure reliability math is unit-tested
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. Extends human_reviews to support blind multi-rater rounds. Provides the denominator that makes US-326's accuracy numbers meaningful ('how good is good?'). DONE (2026-06-02): pure lib/irr.ts — pairwiseAgreement (agreement-within-0.5 + MAE over reviewer pairs), krippendorffAlphaInterval (handles >=2 raters + missing data), consensusScores, compareAiToHumans (AI vs human consensus + ai_meets_human), computeIrrReport (+ sufficient_sample gate). 12 unit tests incl. a hand-computed Krippendorff oracle (alpha ~0.390) and a negative-alpha case. Migration 00070: reliability_studies + reliability_study_items + reliability_ratings (admin RLS, is_admin() read, service-role writes). Admin endpoints on /api/admin/grading/reliability/*: create/list studies, add items, BLIND per-reviewer queue (never returns AI grade or others' ratings), upsert rating (open-study + membership guarded), close, and report (computes IRR via irr.ts incl. AI-vs-consensus). Admin page src/pages/admin/reliability.tsx (create study, add submissions, blind-rate my queue, view report incl. 'AI meets/beats experts' badge) + route + admin-layout nav. Transparency (US-326) public report extended: loadCitableReliability() surfaces the most recent CLOSED study's human baseline + AI comparison only when sufficient_sample, rendered as a new 'How good is good?' section. Edge suite 90 passed/0 failed; frontend tsc -b + eslint + build green.

userStories.title: Admin regression-monitor dashboard

userStories.title: Photo tamper-suspicion detection (edited-to-hide-defect) via grading vision pass
userStories.description: As a buyer relying on a grade, I want GradeThread to flag photos that appear digitally edited to conceal a defect (content-aware fill over a hole, clone/heal, localized smoothing inconsistent with the fabric), so that a manipulated photo lowers grade confidence and is reviewed instead of producing a falsely high grade.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading prompt (per-image and/or composite) returns a structured manipulation signal: manipulation_suspected (bool), confidence (0-1), and suspected_regions/tells (e.g. cloned texture, unnatural smoothing near seams/known wear points, mismatched sharpness/noise, halo/warping)
A suspected-manipulation result reduces the grade confidence and sets needs_human_review=true (reuses the existing low-confidence review routing)
The signal is persisted on grade_reports (new column/jsonb) and exposed to admins; it is treated as a confidence-lowering signal, NOT a hard 'fake' verdict
Benign edits explicitly do NOT trigger it (crop, rotation, exposure/levels/white-balance, background removal) — only deception-pattern edits; tuned to keep false positives low
Golden eval cases include at least one edited-to-hide-defect example so prompt changes can't silently regress the detector
Edge typecheck + tests pass
userStories.notes: BUILT (claude/grading-platform-authority-ornp9). Per-image vision pass now returns an authenticity block (manipulation_suspected/confidence/tells); aggregateAuthenticity() synthesizes the garment-level signal, caps confidence below the review threshold, and forces needs_human_review. Persisted to grade_reports.image_authenticity (migration 00061) + moderation flag. Unit-tested (authenticity_test.ts). BUILD-NEW. Highest-value, lowest-effort anti-fraud item: rides existing confidence scoring + human-review queue (00049) + image_validity. NOTE: classic pixel forensics (ELA/noise) are unreliable on our images because the client compresses/re-encodes before upload (src/lib/image-utils.ts), so the vision model is the right detector here. Surface on the certificate via US-328. Extend ai-grading.ts + grading-pipeline.ts.

userStories.title: Perceptual-hash photo-reuse & duplicate detection
userStories.description: As the platform, I want to fingerprint every uploaded grading photo with a perceptual hash and detect when the same image is reused across submissions or sellers, so that stolen listings, recycled photos, and stock images are flagged for review instead of being graded as a fresh item.
acceptanceCriteria: A perceptual hash (pHash/dHash) is computed for each grading image at ingest and stored with the image record
On submission, near-duplicate matches against prior images are detected via Hamming distance within a tunable threshold (robust to our compression/resize)
A match to a DIFFERENT user/submission flags the submission for review with the matched reference(s); a match to the SAME user's prior item is informational (legit relist)
Cross-tenant matching is privacy-careful: only an internal flag + reference id is surfaced to admins/owner, never another user's identity or photo to the submitter
Hashing + distance logic is unit-tested with transformed (resized/recompressed) copies; tenant isolation preserved
userStories.notes: BUILT (claude/grading-platform-authority-ornp9). Client computes a 64-bit dHash on the orientation-corrected canvas (image-utils.computeDHash), threaded through photo-upload + new-submission + bulk-submission as a 'phashes' field; grade.ts validates + stores submission_images.phash (migration 00062). grading-pipeline calls detectPhotoReuse (lib/photo-reuse.ts) — bounded Hamming scan over recent hashed rows; a CROSS-ACCOUNT match flags the submission for moderation, same-account is informational. Pure hammingHex unit-tested (photo-reuse_test.ts). Threshold tunable via GRADING_REUSE_MAX_HAMMING (default 10). NOTE: FlipDesk item_photos use a separate uploader and are out of scope here. BUILD-NEW. Stronger 'stolen/stock photo' signal than EXIF and fully under our control.

userStories.title: Screenshot / watermark / other-platform-chrome detection
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want grades to flag when a 'photo' is actually a screenshot of another listing or carries another marketplace's watermark/UI chrome, so that re-photographed or scraped listings don't pass as first-party photos.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading vision pass flags screenshot indicators (UI chrome, status bars, other-platform branding) and visible watermarks/text overlays
Flagged images lower confidence and route to review; the reason is recorded
False positives on legitimate on-garment graphics/branding are minimized (distinguish garment print from app/watermark overlay)
Signal persisted and visible to admins; tests cover representative cases
userStories.notes: BUILT (claude/grading-platform-authority-ornp9) alongside US-336: the per-image authenticity block includes screenshot_or_watermark + reason; aggregated into image_authenticity.screenshot_or_watermark_detected, which also lowers confidence + routes to review. BUILD-NEW. Small add-on to US-336 (same vision pass / output schema). Catches scraped-listing fraud the tamper detector misses.

userStories.title: Original-image + EXIF retention pipeline (forensic/provenance enabler)
userStories.description: As the platform, I want to optionally retain the original uploaded file and capture its EXIF metadata BEFORE client-side compression, so that forensic analysis and provenance features have the untouched data they need (today the canvas re-encode strips EXIF and forensic signal).
acceptanceCriteria: Client reads EXIF from the original file (camera make/model, DateTimeOriginal, GPS if present) before compression and submits it as structured metadata alongside the compressed image
Optionally the original (uncompressed) file is uploaded to a restricted, non-public storage path for server-side forensic use, gated by config/plan and a clear privacy disclosure
EXIF is stored on the image record (nullable; absence is normal and never penalized on its own)
Privacy: GPS/metadata handling is disclosed, access-controlled, and never exposed publicly or to buyers; retention policy defined
No regression to the existing fast compressed-upload path; tenant isolation preserved
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. GATING ENABLER for US-340/US-341 — current pipeline (image-utils.ts compressImage) destroys EXIF + forensic artifacts. Add an EXIF reader (e.g. exifr) client-side; store on submission_images/item_photos. Privacy-sensitive: requires policy + disclosure update.

userStories.title: Verified Capture: opt-in provenance booster + badge
userStories.description: As a seller who wants maximum buyer trust, I want an opt-in 'verified capture' path (in-app capture or originals with intact, recent, consistent EXIF) that RAISES grade confidence and earns a trust badge, so that controlled provenance is rewarded rather than absence of metadata being punished.
acceptanceCriteria: An opt-in capture flow preserves provenance (in-app capture session and/or original-with-EXIF upload) and verifies recency/consistency (timestamp within window, consistent device, no reuse match from US-337)
A passing verified-capture submission earns a 'Verified Capture' badge shown on the certificate and (optionally) the verified-seller profile
Verified capture is a POSITIVE signal that can raise confidence; never required, and missing EXIF alone is never a negative
Anti-gaming: spoofed/edited EXIF and reused photos do not earn the badge; checks are server-side
Privacy disclosure covers what provenance data is captured and how it's used
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. The PSA-style 'control the intake' analog: provenance as a booster + badge, not a fraud gate. Depends on US-339. Ties to certificate (US-328) + Verified Seller profile (US-057).

userStories.title: Server-side forensic/ML manipulation pass on original images
userStories.description: As the grading team, I want a server-side forensic/ML analysis (ELA, noise/PRNU consistency, copy-move/clone detection, learned inpainting detectors) run on RETAINED ORIGINAL images, so that manipulation detection has a second, pixel-level line of evidence beyond the vision model — only where originals are available.
acceptanceCriteria: When an original (uncompressed) image is retained (US-339), a forensic pass produces per-region manipulation scores and an overall tamper likelihood
Forensic output is fused with the US-336 vision signal into a single tamper assessment that adjusts confidence/review routing
Runs only on originals (skips compressed-only submissions cleanly) and is cost/throughput bounded
False-positive guardrails: benign global edits don't score as manipulation; thresholds tuned against a labeled set
Pure scoring/fusion logic is unit-tested
userStories.notes: BUILD-NEW. Heaviest item; depends on US-339 (originals) and complements US-336. Forensics are unreliable on our compressed images, so this is explicitly originals-only. Watch FP rate + storage/compute cost.

userStories.title: Moderation queue: surface fraud-signal context for flagged submissions

Typecheck + build pass

Enriched the EXISTING moderation queue (src/pages/admin/moderation.tsx — it already had approve/reject/ban) to fetch grade_reports and surface per-flag-type badges (Possible photo edit / Screenshot-watermark / Reused photo / May not be clothing), grade+confidence, authenticity tells, and the photo-reuse note, with a link to the certificate. userStories.title: Submitter grade-dispute path with predefined reasons + status notifications

Notification calls target the edge (functions) host correctly; typecheck + build pass

userStories.title: Block SSRF in public API image-URL fetch
userStories.description: As the platform, I must not fetch attacker-controlled URLs server-side, so an API-key holder cannot pivot to internal services or cloud metadata via the grade-submission image URL.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/grades (api-v1.ts ~L214) rejects non-https URLs and resolves+validates the target IP is public (block RFC1918/loopback/link-local/169.254.169.254) before fetching

Regression test fetching http://169.254.169.254 and an RFC1918 host asserts rejection
userStories.notes: Done 2026-06-03. New lib/ssrf.ts (assertPublicUrl + safeFetch): resolves DNS, blocks RFC1918/loopback/link-local/169.254.169.254/CGNAT/reserved + IPv6 ULA/link-local/mapped-private, disables auto-redirects (re-validates each hop), caps body size+timeout. api-v1.ts image fetch now uses safeFetch; non-https/malformed image URLs rejected up front with 400. Tests: src/tests/ssrf_test.ts (metadata + RFC1918 + IPv6 + redirect cases). Deno can't run here (deno.land/esm.sh blocked by network policy) — tests written to convention, logic review-verified.

userStories.title: Validate/allowlist outbound webhook delivery URLs (SSRF)

Delivery does not follow redirects to private ranges; stored response bodies are capped/redacted

userStories.notes: Done 2026-06-03. webhook_url validated at set-time (PATCH /webhook via assertPublicUrl — https-in-prod + private-range block) and at delivery-time (webhook-delivery.ts re-validates before each POST, guards DNS-rebinding) with redirect:"manual" so a 3xx can't bounce delivery to an internal host; response body already capped to 500B. userStories.title: Authenticate + dedup the eBay account-deletion webhook

userStories.title: Harden eBay OAuth-token encryption (AAD binding + rotation)
userStories.description: As the platform, stored eBay tokens must be bound to their owner and the key must be rotatable, so a single key leak or swapped ciphertext is contained.
acceptanceCriteria: AES-GCM additionalData binds ciphertext to the owning user_id

userStories.title: Retry critical webhook handlers on DB write failure
userStories.description: As the platform, a transient DB failure on a critical billing event must trigger a Stripe retry, so subscription state transitions aren't permanently lost.

userStories.title: Key pending-downgrade clearing on the schedule, not plan-string

Test: downgrade to a yearly plan clears pending state
userStories.notes: [P3][Billing] DONE 2026-06-04. Pending-downgrade clearing was keyed on an exact plan-STRING match (plan === pending_flipdesk_plan), which couldn't tell 'schedule just attached' from 'phase activated' and MISSED interval-only downgrades (pro/monthly -> pro/yearly, where the plan string never changes -> the 'Downgrade scheduled' banner stuck forever). Now keyed on the Stripe SCHEDULE lifecycle via pure shouldClearPendingDowngrade (lib/pending-downgrade.ts): Stripe releases the schedule (sub.schedule -> null, or a different id) once the final phase activates, so we clear when the tracked schedule is GONE AND the resolved plan+interval match the target — and, as a reconcile, when pending_effective_at has passed and the schedule is gone (so stale pending can't stick). handleSubscriptionChange computes incomingScheduleId from sub.schedule and feeds it + the pending_* columns (added pending_flipdesk_interval/pending_schedule_id/pending_effective_at to USER_SELECT) into the helper; the existing cleared-block already nulls all four pending_* columns. Tests: tests/pending-downgrade_test.ts (attach keeps banner; plan-downgrade activation clears; interval-only yearly activation clears; different/absent schedule id; stale reconcile; gone-but-unmatched-and-not-passed keeps). Node port 8/8; frontend tsc clean.

userStories.title: Growth suite database schema & TypeScript types
userStories.description: As a super admin, I need the data model for the Promote/Growth suite so segments, campaigns, announcements, and referrals can be persisted and queried. updated_at triggers via existing public.set_updated_at()
src/types/database.ts exports Row/Insert/Update for every new table plus the new enum unions, wired into the Database interface

userStories.title: APNs push-send infrastructure (complete the iOS pipe)
userStories.description: As the platform, I need a server-side APNs sender so the already-registered iOS device tokens (push_device_tokens) can actually receive pushes — today registration exists but no send path does. Build lib/apns.ts: token-based (.p8) auth with ES256 JWT (cached <60min), HTTP/2 send to api.push.apple.com / api.sandbox.push.apple.com keyed by token environment, per-token result handling, and pruning of 410/BadDeviceToken responses (is_active=false). Gracefully no-ops when APNS_* env is unset (mirrors email/GSC). Exposes sendPushToUser(userId, payload) fanning out across the user's active tokens, used by transactional notifications and campaigns.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/apns.ts signs ES256 JWT from APNS_KEY_P8/APNS_KEY_ID/APNS_TEAM_ID, caches token, targets prod/sandbox by row environment
sendPushToUser() fans out to active push_device_tokens rows and returns per-token delivery results
410 / Unregistered / BadDeviceToken responses flip push_device_tokens.is_active=false
No-ops cleanly (returns sent=0) when APNS env not configured — never throws
Wired into the 4 defined iOS categories where a server trigger already exists (e.g. token.expiring, item.review_needed) best-effort
Typecheck passes (deno check)
userStories.notes: [P1][Growth] BUILT 2026-06-05: lib/apns.ts sender + lib/transactional-push.ts wired into all 4 iOS categories where a server trigger exists: item.review_needed (grading-pipeline.ts), token.expiring (flipdesk-ebay oauth/refresh catch), sale.created (flipdesk-ebay order sync), payout.cleared (ebay-payout-dedup). All fire-and-forget; no-ops when APNS_* unset.

userStories.title: Multi-channel campaign composer & send engine
userStories.description: As a super admin, I want to compose a message and broadcast it to a saved segment across email, in-app, and iOS push, so I can run promotions and announcements at scale. A campaign = subject/title + body (+ optional CTA url) + channel set + target segment + send-now or scheduled. The send engine resolves the segment to users, writes a campaign_recipients row per user/channel, and dispatches email (sendBroadcastEmail with unsubscribe), in-app (notifications insert), and push (sendPushToUser). Sending is throttled/batched, idempotent (won't double-send a recipient), respects notification_preferences opt-outs for the marketing category, requires a fresh MFA step-up, and is fully audit-logged.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/growth/campaigns creates a draft; POST /campaigns/:id/send dispatches (step-up required)
Send resolves segment, batches recipients, writes campaign_recipients ledger, dispatches per selected channel
Respects marketing opt-out in notification_preferences for email + push (transactional unaffected); in-app always allowed
Idempotent: re-running send skips recipients already marked sent for that channel
Scheduled campaigns dispatched by POST /api/jobs/growth-dispatch cron (job-secret gated, outside /api/admin)
email.ts sendBroadcastEmail adds a working unsubscribe/manage-preferences link
src/pages/admin/growth/campaigns.tsx: list, compose (channel + segment picker), schedule, send, per-campaign delivery stats
